## Security verdict: PASS WITH NOTES

PR #199, exact head `e454bd6a501d01514b65527f146fe061d10f7188`.

The complete three-file diff and directly dependent spawn-path construction were source-reviewed under C33. No new in-scope security vulnerability was identified.

| # | Severity | File | Lines | Vulnerability | Confidence |
|---|----------|------|-------|---------------|------------|
| - | - | - | - | No new in-scope vulnerability identified | - |

Production evidence paths use a daemon-minted spawn ID: `s-` plus 16 OS-random bytes in hex, separate from caller-selected seat/window names (`crates/daemon/src/http/mod.rs:1449-1453,4130-4141`). Status/log paths sit under the existing temp-directory spawn root (`:1531-1535,1774-1780`).

`write_exit_status` changes only the extension to status.partial, preserving the same parent directory, writes numeric exit text, then renames to the final path (`crates/cli/src/main.rs:4054-4062`). No shell interpretation or caller-provided staged basename was added. On the Unix review target, rename replaces the destination directory entry rather than writing through a destination symlink.

Permission/symlink qualification: the staged write still uses ordinary filesystem write semantics, follows a pre-existing staged-path symlink and creates files under inherited directory permissions/umask. No ownership, no-follow or private-directory hardening is introduced. Same-user manipulation is out of scope under C33; this verdict does not certify a spawn directory writable by another account.

The helper returns write/rename errors. Normal exit logs a publication error; the failed-launch 127 path still ignores status-publication errors, as it previously ignored direct-write errors. A failed rename can leave the partial file and no published status. These are reliability qualifications, not a demonstrated new security exploit.

The reader treats missing or whitespace-empty status as no exit yet and still errors on malformed nonempty content (`crates/daemon/src/http/mod.rs:1783-1816`). Tests pin empty/valid/malformed behavior and replacement of an open old file with complete new content and no staged file (`crates/daemon/src/http/tests.rs:3408`; `crates/cli/src/main.rs:5045`); they were read, not locally executed.

No new C19/C21 disclosure was identified. GitHub metadata and the independent remote pull ref agree on the full reviewed SHA; GitHub reports CLEAN. CI run `42542206709` and Delivers run `42542206655` both identify this SHA and success.

No local builds, tests, spawn/status-file experiments, permission changes, credential reads or mutations were performed.
